config.title: Build route guards for auth only pages

intro.title: Build route guards for auth only pages
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple route guard to protect a private page, ensuring only authenticated users can access it. You'll learn how to use conditional logic to check for authentication and redirect users if they are not logged in. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, conditional statements, and basic routing simulation. This hands-on exercise will help you understand how to control access to specific parts of a web application securely.
intro.usecase: Route guards are essential security patterns in modern web applications that control access to sensitive areas. You'll implement them to protect user dashboards, admin panels, and payment pages—ensuring only authenticated users can view their personal data or perform transactions. For example, banking apps use route guards to prevent unauthorized access to account transfer screens, while e-commerce sites guard checkout flows until users log in. As a developer, you'll apply these patterns whenever building applications with user accounts, subscriptions, or role-based permissions.

objectives: Implement a route guard function that checks authentication status
Apply the route guard to protect specific pages from unauthorized access
Construct conditional rendering logic to display content based on authentication state
Configure navigation behavior to redirect unauthenticated users to a login page
Integrate route guards with existing authentication state management
Manipulate browser history to control user flow during authentication checks
Initialize route protection on application load and route changes

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a div.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns a JSX div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns a div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named App and returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not correctly defined. It should be a function named App that returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create an isAuthenticated state variable initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with false as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into isAuthenticated and setIsAuthenticated.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [isLoggedIn, setIsLoggedIn] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has an isAuthenticated state variable that tracks whether the user is authenticated.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with false, and the returned array is destructured into isAuthenticated and setIsAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with false and destructuring both the value and setter.
steps.feedbackWrong: call useState(false) and destructure the result into [isAuthenticated, setIsAuthenticated].

steps.title: Create login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named handleLogin that sets the isAuthenticated state to true.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsAuthenticated with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleLogin function is defined inside the App component that updates the authentication state.
successCriteria: The handleLogin function is defined and calls setIsAuthenticated(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named handleLogin and calls setIsAuthenticated(true).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleLogin function is not properly defined. It should be inside the App component and update the isAuthenticated state.

steps.title: Create route guard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthGuard that takes children as props and conditionally renders them based on isAuthenticated.
steps.hint: Define a component that receives props and returns either the children or a fallback message.
steps.expectedOutcome: An AuthGuard component is defined that can be used to protect routes by checking authentication.
successCriteria: AuthGuard component is created, takes children prop, and conditionally returns children based on isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the AuthGuard component. Make sure it takes children as a prop and conditionally renders them based on isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthGuard component isn't properly defined. It should be a functional component that receives children and conditionally renders them.

steps.title: Implement authentication check in guard
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthGuard component, add logic to check if isAuthenticated is true. If authenticated, return the children prop; otherwise, return a paragraph with the text 'Access denied. Please log in.'
steps.hint:
Use a conditional statement (if/else or ternary) to check the isAuthenticated prop. Return children when true, and a

element with the denial message when false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthGuard component now conditionally renders children or an access denied message based on the isAuthenticated prop.
successCriteria: AuthGuard returns children when isAuthenticated is true, and returns a paragraph with 'Access denied. Please log in.' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some logic, but make sure to return the children prop when authenticated and a paragraph with the exact denial message when not.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthGuard component doesn't yet implement the authentication check. Add conditional logic to return children or an access denied message.

steps.title: Add login/logout buttons to App
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add two buttons: one with text 'Login' that calls handleLogin when clicked, and another with text 'Logout' that calls handleLogout when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on each button to call the appropriate handler function. Place both buttons inside a container like a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will return a div containing two buttons that trigger authentication state changes when clicked.
successCriteria: Two buttons are present in the return statement: one with text 'Login' and onClick={handleLogin}, and another with text 'Logout' and onClick={handleLogout}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have both a 'Login' button calling handleLogin and a 'Logout' button calling handleLogout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not correctly wired. Ensure you add both buttons with the correct onClick handlers inside the return statement.
